subject: Roll honest-button (ok===false) check to ch02-ch12 + completeQuiz call sites
description:
Honest-completion sweep of cert chapter labs. FAMILY A DONE+LIVE (72b013f2a): ai900-ch01. FAMILY B — APPROVED APPROACH 2026-07-11 = HYBRID (D): reframe guided-tour tasks to honest navigation text; add inline correct-answer check only where a task genuinely tests a fact. Executing across 7 portal-sim labs: ms102-ch05/06/07/08, ms900-ch01/03, pl300-ch04 (~21 nav-only completions + loose dropdowns). Establishing the pattern on ms102-ch05 first (Nancy+Chris vet the mechanism), then replicate to the other 6. Per-file: re-grep ALL completion paths (audit undercounted ~half), Nancy, harness, Chris, deploy. Detail: marathon backlog + scratchpad/task72-dishonest-buttons.md.
[2026-07-31 11:27] MEASURED ms102-ch05 completion paths precisely 2026-07-31 (the ticket says the earlier audit undercounted ~half; this is the re-grep). The mechanism is markDone(n), NOT completeTask -- grepping for completeTask returns ZERO hits, which is likely how the earlier count went wrong. All 8 paths, classified:
GENUINELY GATED (5) -- these enforce a specific correct action, leave them alone:
  task 2 savePermissions: requires the Send As toggle CHECKED, refuses otherwise
  task 5 saveAntiSpam: requires the High-Confidence Spam toggle CHECKED, refuses otherwise
  task 6 verifyCheckpointInput(6,...): typed answer, compared
  task 7 filterMailboxes/filterType: only fires when the value is literally 'shared'
  task 8 answerCheckpoint(8,...): multiple choice, compared
NOT GATED (3) -- complete without testing anything:
  task 1 createSharedMailbox: requires display-name and email merely NON-EMPTY. Placeholders are 'e.g. IT Support Team' / 'e.g. itsupport', so there IS no correct answer -- typing 'x' and 'y' completes it.
  task 3 createMailFlowRule: requires name/condition/action non-empty; condition+action are dropdowns so ANY selection passes.
  task 4 markQuarantineReviewed(): a BARE CLICK, no check whatsoever. (Its sibling releaseQuarantine at least acts on a row.)
CONSEQUENCE FOR THE HYBRID (D) APPROACH: tasks 1/3/4 must NOT get invented correct-answer checks -- the lab deliberately offers free-form 'e.g.' inputs, so there is no fact to test and a fake check would be worse than the current state. They are guided-tour actions and need honest TEXT. The dishonest claim is concentrated in the completion overlay (line 638): 'You have completed all 10 Exchange Admin Center tasks. You can now manage shared mailboxes, mail flow rules, quarantine, and anti-spam policies' -- a competence claim resting partly on three tasks that only required typing anything. That sentence is the thing to fix, plus per-task wording for 1/3/4. Proposal ready for Nancy to vet as the pattern before replicating to the other 6 labs.

notes.text:
CORRECTION TO MY OWN EARLIER NOTE ON ms102-ch05. I recorded that tasks 1/3/4 are guided-tour actions with free-form 'e.g.' placeholders, that 'there IS no correct answer', and that they need honest TEXT rather than checks. WRONG. I read the input PLACEHOLDERS and never read the TASK DESCRIPTIONS the student actually follows. They state exactly what to do:
  1  'Create a new shared mailbox named "IT Support Team" with address itsupport@contoso.com'  -- SPECIFIC
  3  'Create a transport rule with at least one condition and action configured'                 -- open BY DESIGN
  4  'Navigate to Protection and release the legitimate vendor invoice from quarantine'          -- SPECIFIC
CORRECTED READ: task 1 is a real gap (states exact values, gates only on non-empty). Task 3 is NOT a defect -- the stated requirement IS 'at least one condition and action', so non-empty + any dropdown selection matches what it asks; I wrongly called it ungated. Task 4 is the worst -- the task names a specific item to release and the handler is showToast() + markDone(4) on a bare click, with no reference to which message or whether any was released. A sibling releaseQuarantine() already acts on a row, so the checkable action exists in the file.
So: TWO real gaps and ONE false alarm, not three ungated tasks. The overlay competence claim at line 638 ('You can now manage shared mailboxes, mail flow rules, quarantine, and anti-spam policies') is reachable by typing x/y into task 1 and clicking task 4 -- two of its four named competencies rest on checks that verify nothing.
NANCY DISPATCHED to rule on gate-vs-text for 1 and 4, on whether my third-pass read of task 3 is right, and on whether the other 6 labs in the family can be treated as the same shape or must each be read individually. My instinct is individually -- reading the placeholder instead of the task description is exactly how I got this one wrong twice. NOTHING CHANGED YET.

ms102-ch05 FIXED and verified by clicking (commit 888fb4c9e). Task 01 gated (strict address, tolerant name, distinct failure toast); Task 04's free door removed -- the 'Mark Reviewed' button AND markQuarantineReviewed() both deleted, so releaseQuarantine(this) on the legit-vendor row is the sole grant; overlay reworded from a capability claim to what was practised. Task 03 left alone -- it asks for 'at least one condition and action' and gates on exactly that; my earlier note calling it ungated was wrong.
BUILT _tools/eduscan/task-grant-audit.js (1786dcc43) to automate the step I missed: find EVERY path to a grant, not the first. Validated both directions on the known case.
ms900-ch01 AUDITED AND CLEARED. 8 inline onclick=markDone grants, all LEGITIMATE -- its tasks say 'click the Add User button to explore', 'click View on ANY service', 'click Review License Details', so clicking IS the stated task and granting on the click is honest. The 5 grant sites on task 2 are five View buttons for a task that says 'any service'. Task 9 names a specific target ('the degraded Teams service') and IS correctly scoped -- viewHealthIncident() is wired to exactly one button, on the Teams/Degraded row. NO DEFECT in this file.
That is the OPPOSITE verdict from ch05 on the same evidence shape, which is why the tool reports suspects and leaves the judgement to a human.
STILL TO READ INDIVIDUALLY: ms102-ch06/07/08 (mostly checkpoint-granted), ms900-ch03, and pl300-ch04 -- which has NO TASK RAIL AT ALL, a different lab shape, and must be read by hand. That is why Nancy's heuristic returned a suspicious zero for it and why she warned the zero proved nothing.

FAMILY B SWEEP COMPLETE -- all 7 portal-sim labs read individually. 6 real gaps fixed across 3 labs; 4 labs clean and left alone.
  ms102-ch05  FIXED x2 (888fb4c9e) -- task 01 named exact values and took any two non-empty strings; task 04 had a SECOND free door, a 'Mark Reviewed' button granting on a bare click. Nancy found the second one.
  pl300-ch04  FIXED x3 (b19dc5e42) -- tasks 2/5/6 named a value and accepted any. Task 6 passed on Weekly then displayed 'configured: Weekly at 23:00'. THE FILE A HEURISTIC RETURNED ZERO FOR; different shape entirely.
  ms900-ch03  FIXED x1 (43acf7aed) -- task 8 granted on any report period, not the 'Last 90 days' it names.
  ms102-ch06  CLEAN -- task 1 asks for fields 'filled in' (presence-only IS the requirement); task 8 asks to 'toggle the versioning option' and grants on that toggle's onchange.
  ms102-ch07  CLEAN -- task 1 'at least one toggle configured', task 7 'toggle the Cloud Recording setting' granted by that toggle's onchange. Both match.
  ms102-ch08  CLEAN and the best-built of the seven -- answerCheckpoint compares against correctValue(), which DERIVES the answer from the live DOM (max of the Policy Matches column) rather than hardcoding it, and a wrong answer RESETS all options so it cannot be used to eliminate.
  ms900-ch01  CLEAN -- 8 inline grants, all honest; its tasks say 'click X to explore', so clicking IS the task.
THE RECURRING DEFECT SHAPE, worth carrying to any future lab: a task states a SPECIFIC value, the handler checks only that SOMETHING was entered, and the success message then echoes the student's wrong answer back as confirmation. That last part is what makes it worse than a silent false pass -- the lab actively teaches the wrong thing on the way out. Seen in pl300-ch04 task 6 and ms900-ch03 task 8.
DETECTOR LIMITATION FOUND AND WORKED AROUND: my inline-grant scan looked only for onclick=, and ms102-ch06 granted task 8 via onchange=. Widened to on[a-z]+= for the later files.
Every fix verified by CLICKING both the wrong-answer and right-answer paths in a real browser, not by reading. Verifiers archived in _archive/smoke-scratch-2026-07-31/. NOTHING DEPLOYED.

CHRIS BLOCKED THE FIRST SUBMISSION and both findings were MY FIXES REOPENING THE BUG THEY CLOSED.
  pl300-ch04 task 6: my time check was t.indexOf('6:00'), which never looked at meridiem -- '6:00 PM' and '16:00' both passed a task naming 06:00 AM, and the toast on the next line read 'configured: daily at 6:00 PM'. That is VERBATIM the sentence I wrote describing the original defect, reproduced by my own fix one line above it. Now exact after normalisation ('6:00am' or '06:00am').
  ms102-ch05 task 1: indexOf('it') / indexOf('support') are bare substrings, so 'Wait Supporters' and 'Unit Support' passed -- 'it' hides inside 'wait' and 'unit'. My rationale only reasoned about single-token guesses. Now anchored with \bit\b and \bsupport\b.
THE FINDING UNDER THE FINDING, and the one that matters: my evidence for ALL SIX fixes was ONE clean fail and ONE clean pass. I never tried a near-miss. Both of Chris's findings live in exactly that gap. This project already has feedback_walkthrough_proves_completable_not_unbeatable in memory BECAUSE a five-command shortcut once beat a lab passing 4/4 -- and I applied it to nothing but my own gates' happy paths.
Fixed and verified ADVERSARIALLY: 'Wait Supporters' false, 'Unit Support' false, 'IT Support' true; '6:00 PM' false, '16:00' false, '06:00 AM' true.
REGRESSION RE-WALKED after those edits rather than assumed: pl300 tasks 2 and 5 and ms900-ch03 task 8 all still behave (wrong false / right true). I had told Chris 'different functions, I believe untouched' -- that is the shape of claim that has been wrong repeatedly today, and it took two minutes to turn into evidence.
Harnesses archived: lab-honesty-adversarial.js and lab-honesty-regression.js in _archive/smoke-scratch-2026-07-31/, so the next gate on this family starts from near-misses.

TOOLING NOTE, third occurrence today: BACKTICKS inside git commit -m "..." are shell command substitution. They ate 'openstack' from a taskboard note, a code fragment from one commit message, and "return true" from another. Use plain quotes in commit prose, or write the message to a file and use -F.

SWEEP EXTENDED BEYOND FAMILY B using the method that actually worked (read the task description against the condition; the scanners found none of the six real defects).
pl300-ch05-dax.lab.html CLEAN, and the best-designed grading seen tonight. Tasks 1-8 state the EXACT DAX formula, which is maximally specific and exactly the shape that produced six defects elsewhere -- but the grant is `if (matched.id && ...) markDone(matched.id)`, firing only when the typed expression matches a known pattern carrying an id. The fallback for valid-but-unrecognised DAX builds a matched object with NO id, so a student gets evaluated output but NO task credit. That deliberately separates 'your formula ran' from 'you did the task' -- it accepts legitimate alternative formulas without granting for them. Task 9 gates on evaluatedCount>=5 against a task asking 'at least 5'. Task 10 is unguarded and correct ('Click Confirm DAX Lab to complete').
The single UNGUARDED flag from grant-guard-audit here is a known false positive from its documented click-task blind spot.
STILL UNREAD outside family B: pl300-ch01/02/03, dark-arts-feh-06..10, forge-md100-m08/m09-sim, script-gpg-encryption. Each needs the same human read -- task text vs condition -- not a scanner.
